solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Wat Tyler's wounded by female's light weapon

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for female

indicators.note: wounded means hurt or damaged, so the letters of the rebel's name are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: The leader of the Peasants' Revolt is struck down by a woman wielding some flimsy weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: Wat Tyler led the English Peasants' Revolt of 1381, the puzzle's number. 'wounded' is the anagram signal; the S of Tyler's is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A swatter for flies is a lightweight implement used to strike insects, jokingly called a weapon.

clue.text: Fear health is bad? They believe they can cure you!

definitions.text: They believe they can cure you!

indicators.note: bad suggests something gone wrong or spoilt, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone frets about their health, and a group of confident curers chimes in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges the twelve letters of 'Fear health is'.
explanation.definitionFit: These practitioners claim to cure illness through prayer, touch or spiritual power rather than medicine.

clue.text: Ultimately crazy, the idea peasants not cause of rising

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so take the final letter of each of the next five words

explanation.surface: A wild notion that the rural poor did not start the uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' looks like the revolt again, but here it is dough rising.
explanation.definitionFit: This fungus ferments sugars and gives off gas, which makes bread dough swell up.

clue.text: Without energy, that causes grief

parts.note: w/o is the common written shorthand for without
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Having no energy left is what brings on sadness.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name deep sorrow or distress; woe is the older, more literary synonym.

clue.text: A judge involved in skit upset Asian people

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped up inside, so one piece goes within the other
upset in a down clue means turned over, so the word skit is read upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: A judge is caught up in a comic sketch that offends a group of Asians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns SKIT into TIKS; 'involved in' puts AJ inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the people of Tajikistan, a Central Asian country, so they are an Asian nationality.

clue.text: Tangy pies cooked for country people

indicators.note: cooked means prepared or messed about with, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Spicy pies baked for folk out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country people' looks like rustic villagers, but means the people of a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The inhabitants of Egypt are the people of that nation, so they are one country's people.

clue.text: Lots of unleavened bread: it's apt to go off

indicators.note: going off means spoiling or going bad, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A heap of flatbread is liable to turn stale.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitta is a flat, largely unleavened bread from the Middle East; the plural covers several of them.

clue.text: What comes with a plot for one's retirement?

definitions.text: What comes with a plot for one's retirement?

parts.words: What comes with a plot for one's retirement?
parts.note: retirement here means going to bed rather than stopping work, and the plot is a story's storyline

explanation.surface: Something that arrives with a plot of land when you leave work.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a pension plan and an allotment; really it is a tale read to a child going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A tale told to children as they settle down to sleep has a plot and accompanies retiring for the night.

clue.text: Cross I value

parts.note: to rate something is to value or assess it

explanation.surface: An angry person announcing what they think something is worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like a noun or verb but is the adjective meaning angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cross means being annoyed, and irate is a stronger synonym for angry.

clue.text: Girl I had brought in re trip in stolen car?

parts.note: Joy is a girl's name

indicators.note: brought in means put inside, so one piece is placed within re

parts.note: re, meaning about, is taken as written
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A note about a girl bringing something in regarding a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought in' is the container signal; 're' is the word for about, used here as it stands.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a reckless drive taken for thrills in a car someone has taken without permission.

clue.text: Method of dismissal of nasty white tick

indicators.note: nasty means unpleasant or rough, so these letters are roughed up into a new order

explanation.surface: A pale parasitic bug being sent packing.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batter is out this way by knocking their own stumps with bat or body.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket this is one of the ways a batter can be given out, so it is a form of dismissal.

clue.text: Popular party chief in a part of Asia

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a do is an informal word for a party
Ch is an abbreviation for chief, as in Ch Supt

explanation.surface: A well-liked party leader in some region of Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the old name for the Southeast Asian peninsula covering Vietnam, Laos and Cambodia.

clue.text: High explosive one removed from the shade

indicators.note: removed from means taken out of, so the letter for one leaves the word for a shade

parts.note: a tint is a shade of colour
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A powerful blast that took someone out of the shadows.
explanation.definitionFit: Trinitrotoluene, known by its initials, is a powerful explosive used in blasting and weapons.

clue.text: Queen, meeting communist, was mistaken

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's royal cipher
Red is a common label for a communist

explanation.surface: The monarch blundered by meeting a left-wing radical.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is to make a mistake, so its past tense means got something wrong.

clue.text: Rising, as lover does over time

indicators.note: does over means redoes it the other way round, so the word lover is read backwards

explanation.surface: An ardent suitor gets up, as suitors do, after a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' looks like getting up; it is a noun for an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising is an uprising or rebellion, as in the Easter Rising, so it is a synonym for rebellion.

clue.text: Fool in the morning making the tea

parts.note: an ass is a foolish person
a.m. stands for ante meridiem, before noon

explanation.surface: An idiot brewing up a cuppa at breakfast time.
explanation.definitionFit: This strong black tea is named after the north-east Indian state where it is grown.

clue.text: Escape from conflict, bearing left

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the word for conflict holds the letter for left

parts.note: a fight is a conflict

explanation.surface: Fleeing from a battle while heading leftwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearing left' reads as a direction; 'bearing' means carrying.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking flight means running away, so the noun is an act of fleeing or escape.

clue.text: Prime pieces of loin: usually very dear!

indicators.note: prime means first, so take the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A butcher's best cuts of loin, usually rather expensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dear' looks like costly, which suits the meat, but it is a term of endearment.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an informal, phonetic spelling of love, used as an affectionate form of address like darling.

clue.text: Police crossing unfamiliar lands in wintry spells

indicators.note: crossing means straddling, so the word for police goes round the other piece

parts.note: cops is slang for police officers

indicators.note: unfamiliar means strange or not as known, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Officers travelling across foreign territory during bouts of frost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfamiliar' is the anagram signal on 'lands'; 'crossing' says the police word straddles the result.
explanation.definitionFit: These are short sudden periods of very cold weather, so they are spells of wintry conditions.

clue.text: Commercial that is for all to see, and so long

parts.note: an ad is a commercial or advert
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing, suitable for all

explanation.surface: An advert that everyone can watch, and it goes on a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British cinema rating meaning anyone may watch. 'so long' looks like duration but is a farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: This is French for farewell, used in English as a goodbye, just as so long is.

clue.text: Counting and repeating fibs?

parts.note: the prefix re- means again, so repeating
telling fibs is lying

explanation.surface: Is someone tallying, or just telling the same falsehoods again?
explanation.walkthrough: Read as RE-LYING, it means fibbing again. 'Counting' is counting on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Counting on someone means depending on them, so counting here is a synonym for depending.

clue.text: Irish county's long fields regularly recalled

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the picked letters are read backwards
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: An Irish county's lengthy pastures remembered again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes OGILS from 'long fields'; 'recalled' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a county on the north-west coast of the Republic of Ireland, in Connacht.

clue.text: Teacher, close to despair, is upset

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned over, so the pieces before it are read upwards, backwards
close to means the end of, so take the final letter of despair

parts.note: taken as written; that the letters also run backwards through 'despair is' is a coincidence of this charade, since 'close to' supplies only the final R

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster, nearly in despair, is distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' looks like nearly but gives the last letter, R; with IS that makes RIS, which 'upset' turns over.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils in British schools address a male teacher by this title, so it stands for the teacher.

clue.text: Make rapid progress, then hide in Kentish Town

parts.note: to canter is to move at a brisk pace, as a horse does
to bury something is to hide it

explanation.surface: Hurry along, then lie low in a district of north London.
explanation.walkthrough: Kentish Town is a London district; here it means a town in Kent, the county.
explanation.definitionFit: This cathedral city stands in the county of Kent in south-east England, so it is a town there.
